bss.topic: Movimento abolicionista: Luiz Gama, André Rebouças e Joaquim Nabuco

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que foi o movimento abolicionista no Brasil?
options: Um movimento que lutava pelo fim da escravidão
Um movimento pela independência do Brasil
Uma revolta contra os impostos de Portugal
Um movimento pela criação de ferrovias
questions.answer: Um movimento que lutava pelo fim da escravidão
questions.hint: Pense no significado da palavra 'abolir'.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que cidade nasceu Luiz Gama, em 1830?
questions.hint: É uma capital do Nordeste, muito ligada à cultura afro-brasileira.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que aconteceu com Luiz Gama quando ele tinha cerca de 10 anos de idade?
options: Foi vendido ilegalmente como escravizado pelo próprio pai
Fugiu para um quilombo na Bahia
questions.answer: Foi vendido ilegalmente como escravizado pelo próprio pai
questions.hint: Ele nasceu livre, mas perdeu a liberdade de forma injusta.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como Luiz Gama ajudou centenas de pessoas escravizadas a conquistar a liberdade?
questions.hint: Ele usou as próprias leis do Império a favor dos escravizados.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chamava quem exercia a advocacia sem diploma no Brasil do século XIX, como Luiz Gama?
questions.hint: A palavra começa com 'r'.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Além de advogado, em que outras áreas Luiz Gama se destacou?
questions.hint: Ele escrevia versos e artigos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual era a profissão de André Rebouças?
questions.hint: Um túnel importante no Rio de Janeiro leva o nome dele e do irmão.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destas ideias André Rebouças defendia para depois da abolição?
options: Dar terras e educação às pessoas libertas
Manter os libertos nas mesmas fazendas sem salário
Enviar os libertos de volta à África
Proibir os libertos de votar para sempre
questions.answer: Dar terras e educação às pessoas libertas
questions.hint: Ele pensava em como os libertos iriam viver com dignidade.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual livro Joaquim Nabuco publicou em 1883 contra a escravidão?
questions.hint: O título tem o mesmo nome do movimento.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Que organização André Rebouças e Joaquim Nabuco ajudaram a fundar em 1880?
questions.hint: O nome da organização diz claramente o que ela combatia.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual província brasileira aboliu a escravidão em 1884, antes da Lei Áurea?
questions.hint: Os jangadeiros dessa província se recusaram a transportar pessoas escravizadas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destas formas de resistência foi praticada pelas próprias pessoas escravizadas?
questions.hint: Pense em ações feitas pelos escravizados, não pelo governo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quem morreu em 1882, antes de ver a abolição oficial da escravidão?
questions.hint: Foi o abolicionista que nasceu em Salvador.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique o que significa dizer que houve 'protagonismo negro' na abolição da escravidão no Brasil.
questions.hint: Pense em quem lutou, resistiu e se organizou, além dos políticos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Compare a atuação de Luiz Gama e a de Joaquim Nabuco no movimento abolicionista: em que eram diferentes?
questions.hint: Pense na origem de cada um e no lugar onde cada um lutava (tribunais, Parlamento, livros).

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que é importante valorizar abolicionistas negros como Luiz Gama e André Rebouças quando estudamos a história do Brasil?
questions.hint: Pense em como a abolição costuma ser contada e em quem fica de fora dessa história.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is an embedded system?
options: A computer system built into a larger device to perform a dedicated function
A general-purpose computer used for many tasks
A program that runs in a web browser
questions.answer: A computer system built into a larger device to perform a dedicated function
questions.hint: Think about the word 'embedded': inside something else.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which of these devices is most likely to contain an embedded system?
questions.hint: Look for the device that has electronic controls.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is a microcontroller?
options: A single chip containing a processor, memory and input/output
A cable that connects to the internet
questions.answer: A single chip containing a processor, memory and input/output
questions.hint: It combines several parts of a computer on one chip.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What name is given to the software permanently stored in an embedded system's memory to control the device?
questions.hint: It sits between hardware and software.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: How is an embedded system different from a general-purpose computer such as a laptop?
options: It usually performs only one specific task
It always has a larger screen
It can run any program the user installs
questions.answer: It usually performs only one specific task
questions.hint: Can you install a new game on your microwave?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In a digital thermostat, what is the job of the temperature sensor?
options: To provide input data about the room temperature
questions.answer: To provide input data about the room temperature
questions.hint: Sensors measure things in the real world.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the name for a component, such as a motor or a valve, that an embedded system uses to cause a physical action?
questions.hint: It 'acts' on the world.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which embedded system in a car helps stop the wheels locking during hard braking?
questions.hint: Its name describes what it prevents.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which of these is a typical feature of embedded systems?
questions.hint: Many run on batteries for a long time.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: An embedded sensor in a greenhouse takes a temperature reading every 5 seconds. How many readings does it take in one hour?
questions.hint: How many seconds are there in an hour?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A microcontroller has 64 KB of flash memory. The firmware uses 48 KB. How many KB are still free?
questions.hint: Subtract the space used from the total.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why do many embedded systems need to respond in 'real time'?
options: Because a delay could be dangerous or stop the device working properly
Because they are connected to a clock on the wall
Because users want to play games on them
questions.answer: Because a delay could be dangerous or stop the device working properly
questions.hint: Think about an airbag in a car crash.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why is it usually difficult for a user to change the program in an embedded system?
options: The firmware is stored in memory designed not to be changed easily
The program is written on paper
The program is deleted every time it is switched off
questions.answer: The firmware is stored in memory designed not to be changed easily
questions.hint: Think about where the firmware lives.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Describe how an embedded system in a microwave oven uses input, processing and output.
questions.hint: Think about the buttons, the timer, the display and the heating.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Give two advantages of using embedded systems in household devices.
questions.hint: Think about cost, size, reliability and power use.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain one disadvantage of embedded systems that are connected to the internet, such as smart doorbells.
questions.hint: Think about security and updates.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the main purpose of an article to argue?
options: To persuade readers to agree with a point of view
To describe a place in detail
questions.answer: To persuade readers to agree with a point of view
questions.hint: Think about what 'argue' means.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which feature normally appears at the very top of a newspaper article?
questions.hint: It is the title in large, bold print.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the name for the short line under a headline that gives a little more detail about the article?
questions.hint: It 'straps' extra information onto the headline.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is a counter-argument?
options: An opposing view that the writer considers and then responds to
questions.answer: An opposing view that the writer considers and then responds to
questions.hint: 'Counter' means against.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What word describes the part of an argument where the writer shows why the opposing view is wrong or weak?
questions.hint: It begins with 're-'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is a rhetorical question?
options: Do we really want our parks to disappear?
The park closes at six o'clock.
Park the bike by the gate.
questions.answer: Do we really want our parks to disappear?
questions.hint: It is a question that does not expect a real answer.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these discourse markers is best for introducing a counter-argument?
questions.hint: You need a word that shows contrast.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which technique is used in this sentence: 'Over 70% of students say they feel tired in the morning'?
questions.hint: Look at the number.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which technique is used in this sentence: 'You can make a difference today'?
questions.hint: Who is the sentence speaking to?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which register is usually most suitable for a newspaper article arguing about school uniform?
questions.hint: Think about a wide audience of adult and young readers.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses emotive language?
options: Innocent animals are suffering in silence while we do nothing.
There are 40 animals in the shelter.
questions.answer: Innocent animals are suffering in silence while we do nothing.
questions.hint: Look for words chosen to make the reader feel strongly.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is an anecdote in an argument article?
options: A short personal story used to support a point
questions.answer: A short personal story used to support a point
questions.hint: It often begins 'Last week, I saw…'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the best way to end an article to argue?
options: With a strong conclusion and a call to action
With a list of the writer's hobbies
In the middle of a sentence
questions.answer: With a strong conclusion and a call to action
questions.hint: Think about what you want the reader to do next.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write an opening sentence for an article arguing that schools should start later in the morning. Use a rhetorical question.
questions.hint: Hook the reader by asking something they will think about.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write a short paragraph that presents one counter-argument to 'Homework should be banned' and then rebuts it.
questions.hint: Start with 'Some people argue that…' and then explain why that view is weak.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain why including counter-arguments can make an article to argue more convincing.
questions.hint: Think about how the reader sees a writer who has considered other views.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What do the witches predict Macbeth will become, besides Thane of Cawdor?
questions.hint: It is the highest title in the land.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which king does Macbeth murder in order to take the throne?
questions.hint: He is the king at the start of the play.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In his soliloquy in Act 1 Scene 7, what does Macbeth say is his only motive for killing the king?
questions.hint: He compares it to a rider jumping too high and falling.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is a soliloquy?
options: A speech in which a character speaks their thoughts aloud, alone on stage
A song sung by the chorus
questions.answer: A speech in which a character speaks their thoughts aloud, alone on stage
questions.hint: 'Solo' means alone.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does Macbeth see before him just before he murders the king?
questions.hint: He asks if it is something he can clutch.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What word describes seeing something that is not really there, like Macbeth's dagger?
questions.hint: It begins with 'h'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Who calls on spirits to 'unsex me here' so that she can carry out the murder without pity?
questions.hint: She is Macbeth's wife.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: After the murder, Macbeth wonders whether all of Neptune's ocean could wash what clean from his hand?
questions.hint: It is a symbol of his guilt.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Whose ghost appears to Macbeth at the banquet in Act 3?
questions.hint: He was Macbeth's friend and fellow general.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is Lady Macbeth doing when she says 'Out, damned spot!' in Act 5?
options: Sleepwalking and trying to wash imaginary blood off her hands
questions.answer: Sleepwalking and trying to wash imaginary blood off her hands
questions.hint: She is not awake.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: How does Lady Macbeth's attitude to guilt change during the play?
options: At first she dismisses it, but later it overwhelms her
She feels guilty at first and then forgets
She only feels guilty about Banquo
questions.answer: At first she dismisses it, but later it overwhelms her
questions.hint: Compare 'A little water clears us of this deed' with the sleepwalking scene.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which character finally kills Macbeth at the end of the play?
questions.hint: He is the Thane of Fife.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is a tragic hero?
options: A character of high status who falls because of a fatal flaw
A villain who wins in the end
A comic character who makes the audience laugh
A narrator who explains the story
questions.answer: A character of high status who falls because of a fatal flaw
questions.hint: Think about Macbeth's rise and fall.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: How does Shakespeare present Macbeth's guilt immediately after the murder of the king?
questions.hint: Think about blood, sleep and his fear of noises.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Explain how the 'Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow' soliloquy shows what ambition has done to Macbeth by the end of the play.
questions.hint: Think about how he now sees life and time.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Who is more responsible for the murder of the king: Macbeth or Lady Macbeth? Give reasons for your view.
questions.hint: Consider the witches' prophecy, Macbeth's ambition and Lady Macbeth's persuasion.
